#### Layout

Everything in the tab is laid out the same plain way, with no stray padding or margin anywhere. The header runs the tab's full width, 32 pixels tall, as tall as the body's tab bar, its contents centred up and down in it, with 12 pixels of padding at its left and 8 at its right, and a single 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour along its bottom, the only line in the tab. In it, from the left: the file's path, then 6 pixels after it the unsaved dot while there is one, then at the far right the Wrap button, the Save button, and the close button, 4 pixels apart. All are small ghost buttons 24 pixels tall, the Wrap and close buttons icon buttons 24 pixels square, none with a border. The header has no margin of its own above, below, or beside it: it starts at the top of the tab, directly beneath the tab bar, and its left and right edges are the tab's.
Beneath the header, the file fills the rest of the tab edge to edge, with no margin, border, or rounded corner around it, and nothing between it and the header's line. Its text starts 12 pixels in from the tab's left edge, the same as the path in the header above it, so the two line up, and 8 pixels below the header's line. A message that the file can't be read, or can't be saved, is set in by the same 12 pixels, in a row as tall as its text needs with 8 pixels above and below it.

#### Wrap

The Wrap button, with a wrap-text icon, hard wraps the text at 80 columns, the ruler's, by Piton's rules, changing the file's text itself, as `piton format` changes it. It is an action, not a mode: clicking it, or pressing Alt+Z, wraps once, and the editor never wraps as it is typed in, nor shows a line any other way than as it is. It wraps the lines the selection touches, or, with nothing selected, the whole file. Its tooltip says it wraps long lines at 80 columns, with its shortcut. It is shown only for a Piton file, and is disabled while the file can't be edited yet.
Wrapping never changes what the file says: the file compiles to exactly what it did before, and only lines past the 80th column are touched. A line is broken only where Piton joins it back as it was, so each break is at a single space, which the break takes the place of, in the prose of a multi-line value, the lines after it taking the indentation of the line broken, as consecutive lines of a string block join with one space. Short lines are never joined, and a paragraph is never reflowed: only lines that run long are split, each at the last space it may break at before the 80th column, or, where there is none, at the first after it.
Nothing is broken where Piton would read it otherwise. A line is never broken inside an expression in braces, whether written plain or after a dollar sign, a hash, or an at sign, nor inside an escape wrapper, nor at all inside an escape block or a code fence, whose text is kept exactly. No break is made where the line it starts would begin with `- `, `+ `, or `++ `, which make a list item or a composition line, with `//`, which makes a comment, with a backslash, or with a word followed by a colon and a space, which makes a key; the break moves to the space before or after instead. A line holding a key and its value, `name: value`, a list item, an import, or a declaration is never broken, since what follows it indented would be something else. A comment that runs long is broken the same way, its later lines comments of their own, each begun with `// ` at its indentation. A line with nowhere it may be broken is left as it is, however long.
The wrap is one edit, undone in one step, and keeps the cursor and the selection on the same text. A file the language server reports errors in still wraps, by the same rules. Wrapping doesn't save the file; saving it formats it as ever.

content.text:
Wrap in the editor is now a one-off hard wrap at 80 columns that rewrites the text by Piton's rules, replacing the soft-wrap toggle. All 572 tests pass (1 ignored) and clippy has nothing new.

- **Where it shows:** the button and Alt+Z appear only for Piton files, and are disabled until the file can be edited.
- **What it wraps:** the lines the selection touches, or the whole file when nothing is selected.
- **Editing:** it's a single undo step, keeps the cursor and selection on the same text, and doesn't save the file.
- **Where the rules live:** the new `src/piton_wrap.rs` decides where lines may break, using the Piton grammar to tell prose from keys, list items, declarations, comments, fences and escape blocks.
- **What breaks:** only prose lines and comments past column 80, at the last allowed space before column 80, or the first after it. A long comment continues as `// ` lines.
- **What never breaks:**
  - inside an expression or an escape wrapper;
  - where the new line would start with `- `, `+ `, `++ `, `//`, a backslash, or `word: `.
- **Removed:** the soft-wrap mode and its remembered preference.

One test builds a small project with `piton`, wraps it, builds again and checks every generated reference file is identical. It covers long prose with an expression, an escape wrapper, mid-line `- ` and `+ `, two paragraphs, and a long comment.

**Where I went further than the spec:**
- **Inline lists:** I also never start a new line with `[`, since that could read as an inline list. The spec doesn't list it.
- **Top-level lines:** I never break unindented lines. Declarations written without `export` (like `scope Foo:`) parse as plain prose, so this is how they're kept whole.

The spec and your prompt agree.
